reads.inside: Not loaded into a completed Hermes chat: the shared tryit activation path could not finish isolated-runtime bootstrap in the 30-second executor window; the catalog capability probe loaded register() in isolation. No planned calls were observed.
reads.tests: 363 passed and 1 failed; the failure was a process-writer test blocked when the sandbox refused an AF_UNIX socket.

reads.best: Replaces Hermes's STT provider with a local one and a Desktop UI, with about 30 test files, SECURITY and DESIGN docs and a pinned CI.
reads.worst: The model must be cached by hand, and the stack is large, with profile-by-profile setup that is fiddly.

reads.best: Profile-bound decoding, explicit correction consent and raw-transcript recovery pair a real transcription provider with careful draft-placement safeguards.
reads.worst: Setup is per profile and requires pre-cached model weights; native mode inherits host insertion behavior and cannot reliably interrupt an active decoder.

reads.best: Integrates local dictation into Hermes’s native speech provider with unusually thorough consent, profile ownership, stale-draft protection and no-tool correction tests.
reads.worst: Users must provision cached model weights and opt into profile-wide STT/correction settings, and a successful real speech-to-corrected-draft path remains unverified here.
reads.validate: Passed all 16 catalog checks, no warnings, including declared transcription provider and Python dependency admission; runtime doctor passed.
reads.inside: Loaded smart_dictation transcription provider and smart_dictation_correction auxiliary task, with no agent tools by design; Desktop Native/Contextual UI is shipped. With stt.provider set in an isolated home, three planned terminal probes inside real AIAgent resolved the registered provider, passed a short generated WAV and passed malformed audio. Provider registration/availability succeeded; the valid WAV returned stt_unavailable because no model weights were cached, and malformed audio returned transcription_failed with empty transcript, without a crash or download. These probes called the real registered provider in terminal child processes, not a physical Desktop microphone or a live correction service. Pinned provider: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/metamindedu/hermes-smart-dictation/e62b98787d4d056b8d7c333e05a80c6779f9ba2a/native_provider.py
reads.tests: Passed after declared Python dependencies were installed: 88 Python tests. Initial run without numpy/av had 3 duration-boundary failures and 85 passes, resolved by installing the pinned dependencies. npm test initially passed 87 with 6 skipped; with real Hermes source and its required Desktop test dependencies, all 93 Node tests passed with no skips, including native composer, query client and launcher contracts. UI tests still use simulated media/provider primitives; no successful physical-speech decode or paid correction was tested.

reads.best: A local, offline faster-whisper speech provider for Hermes's own microphone input, with consent-gated, tool-free proofreading that fails closed to the raw transcript.
reads.worst: It adds no tool, its dashboard manifest points to a dist/index.js that is not shipped, four near-duplicate api_v0_N.py files remain, and 3 of its own tests fail against current Hermes.
reads.validate: passed (hermes plugins validate --json: all checks ok); requires_hermes >=0.23.0; 3 pinned deps (faster-whisper, av, numpy) installed by validate --install-deps
reads.inside: Loaded: enable exit 0, doctor OK with 0 tools and 0 hooks; it registers a 'smart_dictation' transcription provider, an auxiliary correction task, a dashboard API (/status, /transcribe, jobs) and a Desktop page. No agent tool to call; a chat with a read_file call completed normally with it enabled. The provider path was not exercised (no microphone/audio or local Whisper model here; downloads are off by design).

reads.best: Native transcription registration plus consent-aware correction and fenced composer insertion improve everyday voice input beyond what a prompt can implement.
reads.worst: Fresh installation needs pre-cached model weights and profile preparation, while provider availability can be true even though transcription still reports stt_unavailable.
reads.validate: Passed catalog admission, enable and doctor with its three declared audio dependencies; no reported warnings; registers a transcription provider and auxiliary correction task, not agent tools.

With stt.provider=smart_dictation, Hermes registry returned the real provider. Availability returned true after libraries/config were present, but a valid short WAV without cached weights returned stt_unavailable; nonexistent WAV returned transcription_failed; call after provider.close returned invalid_owner. All returned bounded error envelopes. Successful ASR, microphone capture and remote correction were not run; ASR in duration tests is explicitly stubbed. Native/contextual composer, consent and draft-owner fences were inspected in source and covered by supplied UI tests. reads.tests: Passed after installing declared faster-whisper/av/numpy: 88 Python tests. npm test: 87 passed, 6 skipped. Initial Python run without audio libraries had 3 failures; all disappeared with declared dependencies. No inference or paid correction test.

reads.best: A fully local speech-to-text provider for Hermes with no secrets, no network, exact-pinned dependencies, readable source for its Desktop bundle and real CI.
reads.worst: Setup is fiddly and hard to demo: the user must set the provider by hand and already have a Whisper model cached, errors are opaque codes, and the README is one dense wall of caveats with a single screenshot.
reads.validate: passed: hermes plugins validate --install-deps exit 0, every check ok, no warnings; its pinned faster-whisper, av and numpy dependencies resolved and installed.
reads.inside: Loaded: enable and doctor exit 0; it registers a transcription provider (smart_dictation) and an auxiliary correction task, 0 tools and 0 hooks, so there was no tool call to plan and the empty-plan chat completed normally. The provider and Desktop composer were judged by reading: every failure path (provider not selected, model not cached, missing or oversized audio, busy) returns a coded error and nothing downloads weights.
reads.tests: failed: pytest 85 passed, 3 failed (the three real-PCM duration tests, which need the av package that is absent from the Hermes environment used to run them); node --test 93 tests, 87 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed. CI in the repo runs three operating systems and rebuilds the Desktop bundle to compare.

reads.best: A substantial observer pipeline combines redaction, session-aware correlation, replay isolation, bounded spooling, Desktop findings and extensive privacy/export tests.
reads.worst: Detection is heuristic and cannot prove exfiltration; pattern-based redaction can miss unknown secrets and bounded queues can drop events under load.

reads.best: Nonblocking observer hooks, evidence labels, bounded retry spools and Desktop findings make Hermes itself visible to existing security operations.
reads.worst: Detection and secret redaction are heuristic, and bounded queues or process shutdown can lose events, so this is neither complete surveillance nor a prevention layer.

reads.best: Native hooks enforce a code-level authority boundary with fail-closed classification and tests covering direct, concurrent and sequential dispatch.
reads.worst: Authorization is only by broad effect category, so an already-authorized capability can still be misused for a different path, recipient or command.

reads.best: Hook-only guard with off/monitor/enforce modes, off by default, covers MCP tools conservatively.
reads.worst: Needs a structured-output classifier model; benefit is hard to see for users; tests live outside the plugin folder.

reads.best: A remarkably product-complete money workflow with approval gating, injection and impersonation defenses, hash-chained logs, a dashboard, demo assets, and extensive adversarial tests.
reads.worst: Its protection is not absolute: pattern-based scam detection and an operator's approval remain critical to safe payment activity.

reads.best: Combines scoped secrets, per-write approval requests, cron refusal, idempotency and tested invoice-specific scam checks into a practical cross-chat product.
reads.worst: Human approval still depends on Hermes policy: YOLO or approvals.mode off auto-approves its prompts; pattern-based scam checks and local hash chains have documented limits.

reads.best: It addresses a high-value agent-specific failure mode at the exact pre-dispatch and pre-delivery boundaries, with fail-closed behavior and tests for secret non-persistence.
reads.worst: Pattern detection cannot guarantee semantic secret discovery, and blocking or rewriting every surface can create compatibility and false-positive costs.

reads.best: It turns Hermes lifecycle data into practical run-quality checks, baselines, incident explanations, and a strong review UI with focused tests.
reads.worst: Several findings are necessarily heuristic from tool names, output text, and historical baselines, so they can miss failures or flag legitimate runs.

reads.best: Catches the unattended-cron failure mode with clear rules, a Desktop and dashboard view and screenshots.
reads.worst: The idea overlaps with generic observability and it edits the agent's answer with a note, with a single test file for 1,600 lines.

reads.best: Reads its API key through Hermes's own secret_scope (not a plain file), explicitly strips admin/tunnel keys from any environment it passes along, and is tested with a stand-in CLI across many real failure scenarios.
reads.worst: Niche audience (users who already run a Tinfoil confidential-computing container) limits how many Hermes users would install it day one.

reads.best: It changes where Hermes runs and keeps the existing tool surface while stripping tunnel credentials and retaining dangerous-command approval.
reads.worst: The small plugin has no bundled tests and requires several separately installed Tinfoil, SSH, container, and key prerequisites.

reads.best: It makes Hermes itself a game-making system, with many native tools, skills, story checks, bot playtests, assets and a desktop surface.
reads.worst: The scope is ambitious and setup is heavy: Godot and Python dependencies are required, platform support is limited, and human playability is not proven.

reads.best: It addresses a distinctive agent failure mode with exact structured intent, chain-id and log checks, conservative verdicts, replay-safe correlation, tests and output correction.
reads.worst: It is limited to Base mainnet and allowlisted payment-tool conventions, so coverage must be configured and expanded for other chains and transaction shapes.

reads.best: Strict, read-only verifier (chain-id check, exact raw amounts, confirmations, time budget) wired into post_tool_call, transform_tool_result and transform_llm_output, tested against recorded real Base transactions.
reads.worst: Narrow scope (Base mainnet, simple transfers, only tools the user names) and no screenshots or video, so it serves few Hermes users.

reads.best: Carefully built spool: O_NOFOLLOW reads, symlink/FIFO refusal, a worker lease, dedup by content hash and crash recovery, all covered by eight tests.
reads.worst: Polling-based folder watcher with a one-job-at-a-time worker and only spool-level tests, nothing that exercises the adapter itself; the audience is people who already script file drops.

reads.best: It makes performance claims an evidence-producing Hermes workflow with output equivalence, noise handling, hooks, and a polished Desktop view.
reads.worst: The hooks fail open and scripts still execute with the user’s permissions, so it is measurement discipline rather than a security sandbox.

reads.best: Connects reproducible before/after measurements and output checks to edit gates and a useful flame-graph Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Interpreter-only filtering still runs arbitrary scripts with user permissions without a native execution approval gate, and the measurement hooks fail open.

reads.best: Live map control, model-generated HUD captions and watch delivery are integrated into Hermes tools and its turn-state hook, making the globe part of the agent workflow [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/EOH/9d433e49645df8ee549b58467876eb1e5daa0f34/gev/hermes_tools.py).
reads.worst: Full functionality requires separately cloning, building and running a compatible globe fork, and its tool snapshots need refreshing when that external catalog changes [setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mojomast/EOH/9d433e49645df8ee549b58467876eb1e5daa0f34/README.md).

reads.best: The implemented route planner, editable board, reversible suggestions, result cards and export workflows make agent work tangible in a polished Desktop surface. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Adolanium/hermes-whiteboard/9151ee902ae7008d1ab47f9398ea7667c569bf2f/desktop/plugin.js)
reads.worst: Hidden sessions retain the user’s tools: prohibitions on file writes, commands and messaging are prompt instructions, while watched tool use is only flagged after it starts. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Adolanium/hermes-whiteboard/9151ee902ae7008d1ab47f9398ea7667c569bf2f/desktop/plugin.js)

reads.best: It separates coverage, test outcome, freshness, and human review instead of treating a green command as proof, and backs that model with tests and disclosure rules.
reads.worst: It is primarily an evidence workflow around existing test runners, so some value still depends on users maintaining meaningful criteria and links.

reads.best: Separates coverage, outcome, freshness and review rather than a single green check.
reads.worst: Audience is mainly developers who track requirements, and it only imports results.

reads.best: It gives Hermes a substantial phone-first control surface through Telegram, with Telegram initData verification and an explicit allowlist-based login.
reads.worst: Its implementation reaches into private Hermes internals and runs a polling alert thread; the wide control surface increases compatibility and operational risk.

reads.best: Signed, key-pinned device pairing with policy caps, approvals kept, ~70 test files, CI and a Desktop pane.
reads.worst: Large, complex codebase (~13k lines) and remote shell execution increase setup and security surface.

reads.best: Its signed device protocol and terminal-environment-provider integration address a meaningful own-hardware agent use case.
reads.worst: At the pinned revision it has neither plugin manifest nor README nor tests, so the catalog entry is not a dependable installable product.

reads.best: Real subagent hooks, optional per-attempt models, terminal-dispatched checks and a Desktop race board make best-of-N coding operational.
reads.worst: Worktree pinning is textual path rewriting rather than containment: relative parent paths and shell navigation can escape it, and MCP writes are not rewritten.

reads.best: Unusually finished Desktop experience with ~370 tests and local-only audio analysis.
reads.worst: Mostly ambience, not agent capability; Linux-first, large 29k-line codebase.

reads.best: Approval-aware delegation, persistent card/session links and extensive integration tests make it a substantive extension of Hermes workflows.
reads.worst: Requires separately installed omp and omp-sessions runtimes and relies on undocumented Hermes kanban internals, making setup and compatibility more fragile.

reads.best: Deep integration ties persistent external coding sessions to Hermes chats and kanban cards, with readable code, extensive tests and a finished supervision UI.
reads.worst: At the pinned commit, Tools.start passes the model-selected mode directly to omp.new, including auto, without the agent_approvals guard used by Tools.mode; external omp setup is also required.

reads.best: It exposes a genuinely novel model-level capability based on forward-pass neuron attribution, with lazy loading, download gates, and substantial unit tests.
reads.worst: The audience is limited to users with compatible local Transformer models and substantial compute, and the large dependency/runtime path remains harder to operate than ordinary plugins.

reads.best: A rich end-to-end testing workbench joins scenario generation, independent review, evidence audits, frozen benchmarks, Hermes memory references, and dashboard views.
reads.worst: The breadth creates a large compatibility and execution surface: generated evaluators can run on the host, parts of the target harness use private APIs, and full autonomous live campaigns remain unverified.

reads.best: Immutable benchmark provenance and validity-aware comparisons provide a serious regression workflow with native tools, background workers and a dashboard.
reads.worst: At the field pin evaluator preflight inherits the full environment and execution approval uses a global rule key; the documented complete autonomous live campaign also remains unverified.

reads.best: Automatic sync holds calendar-originated changes for confirmation, while provenance journaling and a per-profile lock protect job ownership ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrowBe/hermes-jobs/34c0490fcc08d5e0b60cd56d32f3fa1f7317c317/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: Moving one recurring occurrence needs an explicit additional-run opt-in or an experimental skip workaround because the original slot otherwise still executes ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CrowBe/hermes-jobs/34c0490fcc08d5e0b60cd56d32f3fa1f7317c317/__init__.py)).

reads.best: A new kind of agent tool: dynamic detonation with audit hooks, stub imports, time-bomb clock shift and rug-pull diffing, gated by ctx.ask_choice approval and about 83 tests.
reads.worst: Needs Docker on the user's machine, and its headline catalog-wide run and malicious-fixture results rest on private data that cannot be checked from the repo.

reads.best: It connects real edit and verification events to reusable recipes, with approval and replay exposed through operator slash commands rather than model tools [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilPez00/hermes-physis/330e795b92544ff8d7ca9ab3d099d943dbc2185c/tools.py).
reads.worst: The verification hook returns no objection after exceptions such as command timeouts and skips attempts after the first, so it does not consistently enforce a passing check [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ilPez00/hermes-physis/330e795b92544ff8d7ca9ab3d099d943dbc2185c/tools.py).

reads.best: It turns session lifecycle and model-window data into actionable per-session readings and opt-in alerts, with histories, dashboard surfaces, and screenshots.
reads.worst: Token counts are approximate and can be UNKNOWN until enough information exists; much of the live validation is described but the PR contains no test or check results.

reads.best: A substantial local data pipeline distinguishes absent evidence from negative results and tests privacy across search, reports, trends, and research terms.
reads.worst: The vault is unencrypted at rest and defaults to open disclosure, while tool results expose selected health data to the configured model provider.

reads.best: Fail-closed hooks with ~170 tests, a quarantine log and owner-only release commands.
reads.worst: Pattern-based detection that, as its own README admits, novel obfuscation will pass.

reads.best: Replaces Hermes's context engine via register_context_engine, with tests that compress 100 times and check pins never drift.
reads.worst: Pins live in one global pins.json shared by every session and never expire, so facts from one conversation are injected into all others and the carrier grows without bound.

reads.best: Extends Hermes at the terminal-provider layer so shell and file tools share containment, with inspection commands, a self-test, and an HTML audit timeline.
reads.worst: provider.py writes profile.sb inside run_dir and passes that same directory as writable scratch to the policy, allowing a sandboxed command to alter the profile reused for subsequent commands.

reads.best: Memory backup through post_tool_call and session hooks, a restore that saves the current state first, no credential held by the plugin, and 73 tests against a fake client.
reads.worst: signet_drive_save will upload any local file the agent names, with no path allow-list; the 'read-only' /files route can create a share and blocks the event loop; macOS only.

reads.best: The Desktop workflow implements explicit scope and cost consent, installation-bound receipts, redacted drafts, and bounded native folder inspection.
reads.worst: Website assessments require a paid VibeLeak owner key; local checks are limited static patterns, and native acceptance is Windows-only.

reads.best: Its [deliberation engine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abualnassr/hermes-committee/c7ed1b63feee39185aed90eac0d0f9185109e959/committee/engine.py) implements concurrent independent answers, randomized anonymous reviews, quorum checks, and a separate synthesis stage.
reads.worst: The chat tool's [evidence loader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abualnassr/hermes-committee/c7ed1b63feee39185aed90eac0d0f9185109e959/__init__.py) reads model-supplied local paths directly with no allowed-root or Hermes file-approval check, allowing sensitive files to enter model evidence.

reads.best: Fully local visual memory with no cloud upload, real tests and good docs.
reads.worst: eye_forget with delete_files can delete up to 500 original photos without a confirm, and deletion errors are counted as removed.

reads.best: It turns team blueprints, deployment checks, fleet monitoring and rollback into native Hermes operations.
reads.worst: The dashboard has unauthenticated cross-origin actions that start local scripts or deploy teams, and the Twilio integration reads a credential file instead of Hermes secrets.

reads.best: Fail-closed, read-only design with ~140 tests including adversarial ones and stdlib-only code.
reads.worst: A narrow Linux-only tar.gz scope; a script outside Hermes could do much the same.

reads.best: A creative 'GitHub stars into reusable skills' pipeline with correctly-implemented secret handling (agent.secret_scope.get_secret, never raw env reads, verified by its own tests) and genuine new-skill-registration capability.
reads.worst: The README and code comments are saturated with self-referential rule-ID justifications (e.g. 'R05', 'R11', 'R16') and a forensic git-log provenance dispute about a sibling project, reading like it was engineered to satisfy an automated catalog-rule checker rather than to explain the plugin to a user — a polish/trust concern worth a human judge's attention.

reads.best: Registers real platforms via register_platform, reads every slot token through get_secret, fails closed on bad config, and tests token locks, duplicate tokens, ACL replay and media caps.
reads.worst: A niche need, DM-only, installed by copying files by hand, and the README itself says it is not a sandbox between users who share the profile's memory.

reads.best: The bounded checkpoint parser, numeric edge-case tests and guarded remote client make the implementation unusually careful.
reads.worst: It serves a specialist checkpoint-analysis niche and reports numeric weight differences rather than model behavior or quality.

reads.best: A small readable implementation and real-tmux tests cover persistent REPLs, vim keystrokes, screen polling and fast-exit recovery.
reads.worst: All calls share the fixed hermes-pilot socket and ignore session context, so separate Hermes profiles or conversations can list and control each other's panes.

reads.best: The finished sharing flow combines exact reviewed payloads, new-profile-only adoption, explicit confirmations, local cards, and extensive defensive tests.
reads.worst: profile_credentials directly reads the selected profile's .env and auth.json for secret scanning, contrary to the catalog prohibition on reading credential stores, and publishing relies on a vendor CLI login.

reads.best: The read-only, approval-gated design makes a vague gateway failure actionable without silently restarting or killing processes.
reads.worst: It is a narrow pattern scanner with no hooks or live remediation, so detection quality depends on local log/process conventions.

reads.best: Careful engineering: a sandboxed child process with a hard deadline, about 91 tests with CI, and claims that match the code.
reads.worst: Niche diagnostics that a terminal skill with curl and dig could largely cover; it can probe private and loopback hosts and does not support Windows.

reads.best: The bridge behind it is a tested Python package (about 5,000 lines of code and tests), pinned to an exact version, with a token file instead of a pasted key and an emulator-side mount allowlist.
reads.worst: The Hermes plugin itself is only a manifest, an mcp.json and a skill; it needs the emulator installed and running separately, and DOS automation is a small audience.

reads.best: It delivers a polished Desktop surface while reusing Hermes's existing Spotify authentication and token-refresh machinery.
reads.worst: The pinned repository contains no tests and depends on private/internal Spotify integration seams, so compatibility failures are easy to imagine.

reads.best: Deep, citation-backed domain engine that uses only the standard library, needs no API key, caps its cache and Federal Register calls, has about 1,400 lines of offline tests and CI, and states clearly that it is not a compliance determination.
reads.worst: The audience is a small niche (cement and lime plants, EPA air rules), and the plant layer covers only a few industries.

reads.best: Persistent group context and trust-tier hooks address practical limits of using a personal agent in busy chats.
reads.worst: The pinned code re-registers the bundled WhatsApp platform, rebuilds its bridge at runtime and directly reads .env; these conflict with catalog requirements, and the maintainer explicitly declined the listing.

reads.best: The small readable implementation uses public SDK atoms and navigation, cleans up contributions and ships an installed-app verification script.
reads.worst: Counts exclude unmounted rows, and differing runtime and durable IDs can hide background Working state until the session is focused.

reads.best: Candid about limits and uses held-output hook with boundary tests.
reads.worst: README admits it is a development candidate; labelling every reply unverified adds little value.

reads.best: Immutable snapshots and transactional permission consumption keep model-controlled text separate from owner approval and prevent automatic duplicate sends.
reads.worst: Installation requires a separately isolated Linux executor and potentially SSH tunneling, while granted permissions neither expire nor support revocation.

reads.best: Local document generation, source provenance, generation hashes and application holds support a concrete workflow with substantial regression coverage.
reads.worst: The resume importer accepts only supported text-PDF layouts, Linux/POSIX is the supported host, and international provider success remains partly unverified.

reads.best: Real Unix-socket integration tests cover playback controls, safe argument construction, launch failures, and refusing to quit a process the plugin did not start. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emirkaan5/hermes-disko/92941008c78981e935af6744e09ce2d441056e48/README.md)
reads.worst: The substantial DJ engine and Mac setup are external prerequisites, and optional remote control sends its bearer token over plain HTTP. (Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emirkaan5/hermes-disko/92941008c78981e935af6744e09ce2d441056e48/README.md)

reads.best: The lint tool checks manifests, registrations, schema cost, and common security pitfalls without importing the target plugin.
reads.worst: Its audience is plugin authors, and much of its guidance is a skill that can age as Hermes changes.

reads.best: Calendar writes use Hermes approval cards plus attended-session checks, while mocked tests cover conflicts, retries and unattended refusal.
reads.worst: The submitter explicitly reports no live Google test, setup needs a user-owned OAuth client, and duplicate protection is a non-atomic search before insertion.

reads.best: The dashboard connects visual selection, preview, and a persistent Hermes session for an integrated video-editing workflow.
reads.worst: The backend directly reads API_SERVER_KEY from Hermes .env and accepts a plaintext config override, violating the catalog credential route.

reads.best: It packages a focused, practical marketing-research workflow with platform-specific skills and an explicit read-only/cost disclosure.
reads.worst: The entry is configuration and instructional text only; the core search and analysis service is remote, paid, and not testable from the pinned snapshot.

reads.best: Profile-safe get_secret, GET-only client, coded errors, caching for rate limits, tests and a skill.
reads.worst: Serves a small digital-nomad audience, and the composing brief is the only part a skill could not do.

reads.best: Commitment approvals bind to terms or delivery hashes, and the code independently verifies signatures and credit-note arithmetic.
reads.worst: Practical usefulness depends on an experimental external credit network with synthetic units and no settlement; local issued-note state lacks cross-call locking.

reads.best: Readable dependency-free code validates routines before motion, refuses E-stopped moves and bounds camera downloads, with fake-device tests and screenshots.
reads.worst: Physical-device compatibility is prospective, and clearing an emergency stop relies on a model-supplied boolean and skill guidance rather than an enforced human approval gate.

reads.best: Its multi-client simulator, bytecode checks, tested building blocks and backup-aware installer form a substantial addon development toolkit.
reads.worst: Addon Lua executes in-process without an instruction or wall-clock budget, so a looping addon can hang verification.

reads.best: It adds session renewal and approval handling while registering only the pinned tool snapshot and constraining screenshot paths ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brucexu-eth/hermes-phone-use/a2fc998c4a23351d8659654d8db3338a05a8b349/__init__.py)).
reads.worst: The actual phone operation and safety boundary remain in an external Pinky server on a Mac, limiting the plugin's independent capability ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brucexu-eth/hermes-phone-use/a2fc998c4a23351d8659654d8db3338a05a8b349/__init__.py)).

reads.best: Clean and small: the key comes only from Hermes's secret scope, requests have timeouts, errors are per-URL and clear, and mocked tests cover the main and failure paths.
reads.worst: A vendor adapter for a paid scraping service; it does one ordinary thing and spends the user's credits.

reads.best: The pinned revision routes checks through Hermes approvals and the configured terminal backend, disables local execution by default, and tests failures, timeouts, and evidence linking.
reads.worst: No hook enforces delivery blocking: the agent must choose to call the tool, and evidence reads do not verify the stored record hash or chain.

reads.best: Recovery verification checks next-night biometrics and confounders, with closed-loop fixture tests rather than relying solely on coaching prose.
reads.worst: The full wearable-ingestion coaching loop requires separately installed on-disk skills and setup, while the bundled crunch itself mostly combines triage and reports.

reads.best: Reads SOGNI_API_KEY via agent.secret_scope.get_secret, so it follows the catalog's secret-store rule.
reads.worst: No tests seen, needs a global npm CLI install, and there is no spend cap on billed jobs.

reads.best: Handles pagination, unknown-versus-zero traffic, scoped secrets, bounded HTTP reads and schedule recovery with focused tests and no model cost.
reads.worst: It serves a narrow analytics niche, requires manual environment setup, and uninstalling before unscheduling can leave a cron job and script behind.

reads.best: The implementation keeps presentations out of model responses, restricts site origins and requests approval before live disclosures.
reads.worst: It reads and writes the agent private key and delegation bundle directly in plugin-data rather than using Hermes credential routes, conflicting with catalog rule 11.

reads.best: Careful read-only design (GET only, no redirects, 1 MB cap, trades only as review links) with Merkle checks tested against upstream vectors.
reads.worst: A thin wrapper around one niche app's API with a 35-line README, no demo, and a CHARTRUNNER_ORIGIN override that can point it at any host.

reads.best: Documents OAuth, workspace selection, read-only permissions and stale-versus-live accounting data clearly.
reads.worst: The pinned package is only manifests and a skill: the actual service implementation and tests are absent, and tool behavior can change independently of the pin.

reads.best: Implements inspectable unit propagation and depth accounting locally, with a focused UI and no network or credential requirements.
reads.worst: Parsing silently skips malformed tokens, a capped prefix may still return valid without checking the remaining trace, and the only test file is an argument-driven CLI harness without assertions or bundled cases.

reads.best: The plugin implements substantial policy, trace-inspection and emergency-stop logic with extensive security-focused test files.
